# Third-party code

| Directory | Project | License | Version |
|---|---|---|---|
| `libmspub/` | [libmspub](https://wiki.documentfoundation.org/DLP/Libraries/libmspub), the `.pub` file parser | MPL-2.0 | see `libmspub/VERSION` |
| `librevenge/` | [librevenge](https://sourceforge.net/p/libwpd/librevenge/), document interfaces and OLE2 streams | MPL-2.0 or LGPL-2.1+ | 0.0.5 |
| `compat/` | JeffPub 79's minimal stand-ins for the Boost headers these libraries use | GPL-3.0 (this project) | — |

zlib is downloaded at build time when the system has none.

## JeffPub 79 changes

These are the only modifications to the upstream sources. Each is marked with a `JeffPub 79` comment.

- **Long text.** `MSPUBParser.h` keeps the text stream positions of character and paragraph runs as 32-bit numbers. Upstream stores them in 16 bits, which wrap past 64 KB of text, so in any publication with more than about 32,000 characters every story after that point opened empty (a four-page newsletter lost pages 2 to 4). Found by comparing every page with Publisher's own rendering.
- **No Boost.** `compat/boost/*` provides `optional` (on `std::optional`), `cstdint`, `numeric_cast`, a 2-D `multi_array`, and `trim`. librevenge's Boost.Spirit number parsing (`RVNGPropertyList.cpp`) and Boost.Archive base64 (`RVNGBinaryData.cpp`) are rewritten in plain C++.
- **No ICU.** libmspub decodes UTF-16LE and windows-1252 itself. Other legacy codepages go through `libmspub::setDecodeHook()` (`inc/libmspub/jp_hooks.h`), which JeffPub implements with Qt. A small LCID table replaces `uloc_getLocaleForLCID`, and the encoding guess for Publisher 97/98 files defaults to windows-1252.
- **Linked text boxes.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` adds a `jp:text-id` property to each text object, so text boxes that share one story can be linked again on import. Upstream emits the full story into every box.
- **Text direction.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads the OfficeArt `txflTextFlow` property (0x0088) and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes it on as `jp:text-flow`, so rotated text such as book spines imports as vertical text. Upstream ignores it and the text stacks letter by letter.
- **Normal style inheritance.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` gives paragraphs that name no style the document's Normal style (style sheet entry 0), which carries the default line spacing (typically 1.19 sp) and space after. It also reports the spacing in sp as `jp:line-spacing-sp`, including an explicit 1 sp. Upstream falls back to a flat 1 sp.
- **Text outline.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads the character "line" container (0x59): outline color index and width. `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes them as `jp:text-outline-color` and `jp:text-outline-width`.
- **Table cell fills and borders.** Publisher stores each formatted cell's fill, and each ruled line, as a drawing shape with no page placement whose client anchor names the table (see `TableCellFormat` in `TableInfo.h`). `MSPUBParser.cpp` collects them and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` emits them as `fo:background-color` and `fo:border-*` on the cells. Upstream ignores them, so formatted tables import blank. Worked out from four one-change sample files (fill, horizontal and vertical borders).
- **Arrowheads.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes each line's start and end arrowheads (style 1-5 as stored, and size) on as `jp:arrow-start`, `jp:arrow-end` and their `-size` properties. Upstream reads them but never emits them, so arrows import as plain lines.
- **Text Art.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads Text Art's words (0x00C0), font (0x00C5), alignment, size, spacing and settings (0x00C2-0x00C4, 0x00FF), and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` hands them on as `jp:textart-*` with the shape type, unturned frame, rotation and flips (through `drawRectangle`) instead of drawing the warp's guide curves. Upstream drops Text Art.
- **Text-valued properties.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads Text Art words and font, and picture and shape names, as plain bytes of their stated length. Upstream reads every long property as a list, which misreads text and loses the properties that follow it.
- **Master pages and special pages.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` writes each master page's objects once, inside `startMasterPage`/`endMasterPage`, before the pages, and names each page's master as `jp:master-seq`; upstream paints master objects onto every page. Every real page is written, including pages with no objects of their own (upstream drops them). Special pages (envelope, web and the like: up to four entries at the end of the document's page list, recognized by sequence number, a page kind of 0 in the first byte of field 06, or being blank) are left out; upstream recognizes them only by four fixed sequence numbers, which older files don't use.
- **Tabs, lists, strikethrough, letter spacing.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads each tab stop's alignment, the list kind and bullet character from their own sub-blocks (upstream read the container's value, so lists never came through), the numbering punctuation (0x58), strikethrough (0x10), added letter spacing (0x1B) and tracking (0x1F). `MSPUBCollector.cpp` emits tab stops as `style:tab-stops`, lists as `jp:list-kind`, `jp:list-char`, `jp:list-delim`, and the rest as `style:text-line-through-type`, `fo:letter-spacing` and `jp:tracking`.
- **Line transparency.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads a line's opacity (0x01C1) and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes it on as `svg:stroke-opacity`. Upstream ignores it, so see-through lines import solid.
- **Picture settings.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads grayscale and black and white (0x013F) and the color shown clear (0x0107); `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes them on as `jp:picture-gray`, `jp:picture-bilevel` and `jp:transparent-color`, with the stored brightness and contrast as `jp:brightness` and `jp:contrast`. Upstream reads contrast but drops it, and ignores the rest.
- **Picture crops and see-through pictures.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads a picture's crops (0x0100-0x0103) and a picture fill's opacity (0x0182), and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes them on as `jp:crop-*` and `jp:picture-opacity`, page backgrounds included. Upstream ignores both, so cropped pictures came in squeezed into their frames and see-through pictures solid.
- **Shape identity.** `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes every shape's number with its unturned frame, rotation and flips (`jp:shape-type`, `jp:frame-*`), so the importer can bring a preset back as that preset instead of a freeform outline, and can tell which outline belongs to which fill.
- **Hyphenation.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads the story list (Contents chunk 0x65), where a story's record carries a `04` flag when its text isn't hyphenated automatically, and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` marks those text boxes `jp:no-hyphenation`. Upstream skips the chunk. Matched against the PDFs of the .pub files on hand, every file whose line breaks changed agreed with the flag.
- **Style names.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads the first style sheet (STSH 0), keeping every entry inside its section and losing only names when it is damaged, where each style has a name (Publisher's built-in styles have none and a negative id; -1 is Normal), and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes a paragraph's named style on as `jp:style-name`, with the style's own bold and italic as `jp:style-bold` and `jp:style-italic` (bold and italic in a run switch the style's on or off).
- **Bullet size and font.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads a list paragraph's bullet or number size (paragraph property 0x02) and the bullet's font (0x03, an index into the font table), and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes them on as `jp:list-size` in points and `jp:list-font` by name. With `JP_PUB_TRACE` set, the parser also prints the font table.
- **Process colors.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` decodes a fill's process inks from the tertiary properties 0x019F and 0x01A6 (with 0x019E, the color as shown), and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes them on as whole numbers 0-255 (`jp:ink-c`, `jp:ink-m`, `jp:ink-y`, `jp:ink-k`; never as formatted text, which follows the system's decimal separator) when the fill is that color.
- **Locale-proof numbers.** `libmspub_utils.cpp` adds `fixedNumber()`, which writes numbers with a '.' whatever the system's language; it replaces the `%f` formatting of table rule widths (`MSPUBCollector.cpp`) and clip paths (`PolygonUtils.cpp`), which on a German or French system wrote a ',' and turned a 1.5 pt rule into a hairline.
- **Default white fill.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` fills a shape that is marked filled but names no fill color with white, the drawing format's default. Upstream leaves such shapes unfilled, so they vanish (the white stars in a party invitation template).
- **Spot colors.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` reads a fill's spot ink name (complex property 0x01A1 in the extra-properties record, `P2,#<color>,<ink name>`) and `MSPUBCollector.cpp` passes it with the fill's inks as `jp:ink-spot`.
- **Tracing.** With `JP_PUB_TRACE` set, the parser prints style sheets, unknown character properties, shape records, drawing properties (including complex values), the content chunk list (with its free slots), table and cell records, every shape visited and painted, and the text-stream chunk list. This is used to reverse-engineer fields that are still unread.
- Unused librevenge generators and the directory stream are not built.
- **Metadata is optional.** `MSPUBParser.cpp` ignores errors while reading document properties instead of failing the whole import (affects two sample files in Apache POI's test set).
- **Damaged OLE headers.** `RVNGOLEStream.cpp` rejects impossible block sizes instead of asserting (found by Apache POI's fuzz files).
